item: opf#361 (FF-46): sizeAdjust factors for eight proprietary script families, RR-38 basis, measured on the published 0.18 packages
basis: factor = sum(real advances) / sum(replacement advances), fontkit, sample OpenType language, on the corpus samples of the family script that hold the script and that the real font covers

scenarios.single: proposed factor on every run drawn in the replacement, Latin included (policy sizeAdjust semantics in opf-render 0.18.0, verified on Arabic Typesetting below)
scenarios.perScript: proposed factor on own-script text only (Unicode Script of the family, digits of that script included), Latin and common text at 1 (needs a new policy field and renderer change)
scenarios.perScriptLetters: proposed factor on the family script letters and marks only; digits (also Arabic-Indic and Thai digits), punctuation and Latin at 1
scenarios.noOverhangFactor: smallest single factor at which no measured line the factor reaches (own-script corpus and Latin) runs past its composed width natively

ratio: native / preview width of the same line; above 1 PowerPoint draws it longer than the preview composed it
policyFormat: spec/reference/font-policy.schema.json: replacement.sizeAdjust is one number per row; opf-render sizeAdjustFor applies it to every run drawn in the row replacement, whatever its script. A per-script factor is not expressible today.

verification.note: Arabic Typesetting (policy sizeAdjust 0.64) on the published renderer: renderer width over fontkit width of the replacement at factor 1

recommendation.why: Thai lines at 0.70: native / preview 0.90 / 1.01 / 1.09 (the worst is the Thai-digit sample, +8.9 %; 0.76 would remove every overhang). The Latin of the scheme is narrower still (0.57 of Noto Sans Thai), so it keeps 10 to 23 % slack and never overhangs; leaving Latin at 1 (per-script) would make that 37 to 46 % slack, worse than the single factor.
Thai lines at 0.64: 0.95 / 0.99 / 1.08 (Thai digits +7.9 %). Latin 0.88 / 0.94 / 1.02 (one of 300 strings +1.7 %). Single factor is right; per-script would leave Latin 35 to 44 % slack.

Arabic lines at 0.80: 0.92 / 1.00 / 1.14; the two digit samples (Arabic-Indic and Persian digits) overhang 13 to 14 %, the letter samples are within +4 %. Latin of the scheme (0.65) keeps 17 to 23 % slack. Native set 2: 0.805. A letters-only per-script factor would fix the digits (Arabic 0.87 / 0.98 / 1.01) but leave Latin 33 to 38 % slack, so single 0.80 now.

nativeCrossCheck.note: set 2 ink (6 lines); docs/font-fidelity.md opf#523: 10 native lines 0.68 to 0.90, pooled 0.79

recommendation.why: No single factor works. Arabic letters are 0.71 to 0.74 of Noto Naskh Arabic, but its digits are 0.90 to 1.02, Arabic with Latin 0.84 and the Latin of the scheme 0.84 (0.81 to 0.95). At 0.79 every one of the 300 Latin strings overhangs (median +6.7 %, worst +20.7 %, 175 pt on an 842 pt line) and the Persian-digit sample +28.5 %. The smallest single factor without overhang is 1.015, so keep 1 (the wide-erring proxy opf#523 documents). The right fix is a per-script, letters-only factor (0.79 on Arabic letters, digits and Latin at 1: Arabic lines 0.90 / 0.94 / 1.04, Latin 0.81 to 0.95 slack), which the policy format cannot express today.

nativeCrossCheck.note: decomposed jamo lines draw up to 1.9x natively; no factor fixes them

recommendation.why: Korean lines at 1.06: 0.97 / 1.00 / 1.04 (the jamo sample +3.7 %; decomposed jamo draw up to 1.9 times natively, which no factor fixes). Latin of the scheme (0.99) keeps 4 to 13 % slack, the safe direction. Native set 2: 1.049.

nativeCrossCheck.note: line-break paragraphs mix Latin and digits

recommendation.why: Devanagari lines at 1.07: 0.95 / 0.99 / 1.03. Latin of the scheme (0.94 of Noto Sans Devanagari) gets 11 to 15 % slack (safe direction; per-script Deva-only would make it 4 to 9 %). Not reachable by this row: the other Indic scripts draw in their own Noto faces and already overhang at 1 (Telugu up to +33 %, Kannada +19 %, Gujarati and Malayalam +13 %, Bengali and Gurmukhi +10 %, Tamil +6 %); that needs factors on those routes, a separate item.

nativeCrossCheck.note: measured on Ethiopic, drawn by Noto Sans Ethiopic through fallback, which the row factor does not reach

recommendation.why: The row replacement (Noto Sans) only draws Latin: 0.943 on the corpus Latin, 0.939 on the 300 FF-31 strings; at 0.94 Latin lines are 0.97 / 1.00 / 1.03. Ethiopic (Ebrima is 1.07 to 1.09 of Noto Sans Ethiopic on the corpus; native set 2: 1.074) falls back to Noto Sans Ethiopic, which this row cannot reach; that needs a route change or a factor on the Ethiopic route.

Japanese lines at 1.04: 0.96 / 0.97 / 1.15 (combining dakuten +14.8 %). MS Gothic is fixed-pitch, so its Latin cannot follow any proportional factor: at 1.04, 139 of 300 Latin strings overhang over 1 % (worst +13.4 %), against 223 (worst +18 %) today. 1.04 improves both; full fidelity for its Latin needs a fixed-pitch preview route.

rule.definition: smallest single factor F (0.01 steps, rounded up) with native/(F*replacementRuns + otherRuns) <= 1.03 on every counted line; counted = the family script corpus samples the real font covers (letters, digits, punctuation, mixed) + corpus Latn + 300 FF-31 Latin strings, regular and bold; ships no sizeAdjust when |F-1| <= 0.03
notes: Factors are rounded UP to 0.01, so the worst overhang at the rule factor is at most 3 % and usually below it.
MS Gothic has no bold face: its bold lines use the regular advances (PowerPoint emboldens synthetically) against Noto Sans JP 700.
Lines drawn by faces other than the row replacement (Nirmala UI: Bengali to Sinhala; Ebrima: Ethiopic) cannot be moved by the row factor; they are listed under unreachable and not counted.

families.decisionNote: rule factor 1.02 is inside the 1 +/- 0.03 band (and confirmed by the supervisor)
sizeAdjust 1.07; the other Indic scripts are not reached by the row (see unreachable)
rule factor 0.99 is inside the band; Ethiopic is not reached by the row

the 1.19 sample (jpan-combining-dakuten) fails the rule at 1.04 (+14.8 %) and alone needs 1.16; the fixed-pitch Latin (latn-ligatures, 1.37 at factor 1) pushes the rule factor to 1.33, which would leave Japanese lines 10 to 26 % slack
